text.p: Daiwa Europe Ltd. rated Polish drug maker Jelfa SA as a short-term "hold" and long-term "positive" in a report released on Monday.
Daiwa said that after a 40-percent share price appreciation this year, Jelfa's valuation adequately reflected its near term prospects.
"However, earnings growth will start to accelerate from next year and Jelfa should represent an attractive partner to foreign companies in the increasing lucrative Polish market," the report said.
The report said Jelfa had a 5.6-percent share of production in Poland, the largest market in Central and Eastern Europe, with an estimated value of $1.6 billion last year.
It said Poland's pharmaceuticals consumption was low in per capita terms but that it was currently growing at about 10-15 percent annually.
Daiwa said Jelfa would increase net profit to 24.4 million zlotys this year and 32 million zlotys next year from 20.1 million in 1996.
Price-to-earnings would rise to 17.3 this year from 16.3 last year and then fall to 13.1 in 1998, it said.
